title: Sell Mineral Rights in Uriah, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Uriah, AL | Monroe County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Uriah, AL, in south Monroe County? We check your parcel against the Gulf Coast oil trend and Monroeville probate records, then make an offer.
heroLead: Uriah is a small crossroads community in south Monroe County, and most of the mineral interests we see from here trace back to timberland that's stayed in one family for generations.
intro: Monroe County's mineral history runs quieter than the Black Warrior Basin counties further north, but the Gulf Coast oil and gas trend that produced fields like Citronelle to the south has periodically reached into this part of the state, with exploratory leasing and occasional production tied to the deeper Smackover and Norphlet formations. Uriah sits well south in the county, closer to the Escambia County line, in an area better known for pine timberland than derricks.

If your family holds mineral rights near Uriah, whether from an old timber sale, a farm reservation, or a lease that came and went decades ago, we can trace what you actually own and tell you honestly whether it's producing acreage, speculative acreage, or something in between.

sections.heading: Timberland reservations, not oilfield leases
paragraphs: A lot of south Monroe County land, including around Uriah, has been managed as timberland for most of the last century, sold and resold between families and timber companies while mineral rights were sometimes carved out and kept separate. If your family sold or leased land here for pine production, it's worth checking whether a mineral reservation survived that transaction even if nobody remembers discussing it.

We see this pattern often enough in Monroe County that it's close to the default assumption when someone calls us about land near Uriah: a mineral interest tied to land the family no longer farms or manages day to day, sitting quietly until someone checks on it.

sections.heading: Where Uriah sits relative to the oil trend
paragraphs: The Gulf Coast oil and gas trend that includes the historic Citronelle field and the Norphlet gas play runs generally through the counties south and west of Uriah, and while Monroe County has seen exploratory activity over the decades, it hasn't had the sustained development history of Mobile or Escambia counties. That means most Uriah-area mineral interests are priced as long-hold speculative acreage rather than active royalty-producing tracts.

We still check current state permits and any historic well records against your specific parcel before quoting, because pockets of activity have moved through different parts of the county at different times, and it's worth confirming rather than assuming.

sections.heading: What we look at before making an offer
paragraphs: For a tract like most of what sits near Uriah, our review focuses on your net mineral acreage, whether any lease has ever been recorded against it, and how comparable Monroe County transfers have priced recently. We pull records from the Monroe County Probate Court in Monroeville to confirm your chain of title, especially if the interest passed through inheritance rather than a clean recorded deed.

We'll be direct if your acreage falls into the speculative category. That's still a real, saleable asset, just one priced differently than producing royalty interest, and we'll explain exactly how we arrived at our number.

faqs.question: Is there any active drilling near Uriah right now?
faqs.answer: Not typically. Most current Gulf Coast trend activity in this part of Alabama sits further south, so we generally price Uriah-area interests as speculative acreage unless your specific parcel shows recent permits.

faqs.question: My family owns timberland but I'm not sure if we kept the mineral rights when it was managed by a timber company. How do I find out?
faqs.answer: Send us the family names and approximate location, and we'll check the Monroe County Probate Court records for any mineral reservation or severance tied to the property.

faqs.question: Is speculative acreage actually worth anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, though at a different price point than producing royalty interest. We price it against recent comparable transfers in the county and explain our reasoning in the written offer.
